speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) with the increasing need to use Singpass, what measures are in place to ensure privacy and security for users, especially senior and vulnerable citizens, when they depend on third parties who are tasked to assist them to navigate online services and enter their IDs and passwords; and (b) whether the Government will consider maintaining more alternative avenues, such as physical counters, for the elderly to avail of such services without the need for Singpass as they have difficulty keeping up with the pace of digitalisation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Members would be aware that the key element for the delivery of digital services is to get digital identity right.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the case of Singapore, our national digital identity is expressed through Singpass.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For the well over 90% of people in Singapore who have access to a smartphone, I think all of you, particularly in this House, would use Singpass through Singpass Mobile.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I would take a bet, that most of us who use Singpass Mobile have forgotten our password, because we depend on the biometric features of our smartphone to not only authenticate but also to act as a two-factor authentication system.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, these two questions really relate to the minority of Singaporeans who do not have a smartphone.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You will also recollect that in the old days – I said old because it is quite many years ago – Singpass consisted of a user ID and password.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The two-factor authentication system, the second factor was delivered either through an SMS or through a token – we called it the OneKey token.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The challenge with delivering an SMS is that it requires someone to have a phone, otherwise the SMS message with the one-time password will not reach you.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Therefore, these two questions relate to the small minority of people without a smartphone, without a mobile phone and for whom, the use of the token as a second-factor authentication will not be available from the first of April this year.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I want to emphasise, that when we design our digital services, we design them to be accessible, secure and convenient.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We therefore have to have this assurance that after 31 March this year, these services will continue to be available for everyone just as they have been today.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, let me explain how we are adapting our system.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The first thing is, many Members of this House may not be aware of this new system we have rolled out called facial verification.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This allows users who do not have a mobile phone to log into the Singpass system without the help of a third party.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And they do so by using an Internet-enabled computer with a web camera, webcam for short.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The webcam allows the computer to scan your face, the system then verifies that against the biometric information that the Government has on all of us through ICA.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That means, it verifies against the face on record that we use for Identity Card or our Passport.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This allows people to log on and to authenticate to Singpass even if they do not have a smartphone.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the next supplementary question you would ask, what about those who do not have access to a computer with a webcam?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The answer is that if you do not have access to such a device you can access it through kiosks which the Government has rolled out at selected public locations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These locations include all CPF Service Centres, IRAS Taxpayer and Business Service Centre, Our Tampines Hub's Public Service Centre, Geylang East Public Library – I am just going through a list but this list is going to keep expanding.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, in other words, even if you do not have a computer with a webcam, do not worry there is still a physical counter which you can access.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The next point I would make, is that the other modification we have introduced is what we call Multi-User SMS two-factor authentication, in which users can opt and nominate to have their SMS one-time password sent to another Singpass user who has a mobile phone.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This allows a resident – remember without a smartphone – without a mobile phone, to continue to access services with the help of a trusted family member.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For this mode to work, obviously, the key word is trust.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And our system has to make sure that it also protects privacy and security.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Before the nomination of a trusted party is activated, there is a strict process for us to ensure that we have verified identities of both persons, the nominator and the trusted party, explain to them the use of these and to obtain – very importantly – obtain consent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would also emphasise that the person who is nominated would only get the one-time password.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That person does not have access to the services which the actual user is logging on, does not have access to the information or the transactions that the actual user is transacting in.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The next point is that we will provide help for all those who need it so that there will always be able to have access and skills for an increasingly digitalised environment.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Basically, we have to put our money where our mouth is and ensure that no one is excluded simply because of lack of resources.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For instance, we have the Home Access scheme, which subsidises broadband connectivity and a smartphone or a tablet for lower income households especially focused on low-income seniors.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our low-income seniors can go to a SG Digital community hub to apply for support under the Mobile Access for Seniors scheme, which offers eligible seniors a subsidised smartphone and a mobile plan.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I am sure if someone cannot afford that, if they see their local Member of Parliament, we will find ways to help people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, do not worry about access to equipment or devices.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But actually, the greater challenge is skills – digital skills and that is why we have the SG Digital Office, which is supporting seniors to pick up these skills, including the most important skill, is how to use Singpass Mobile.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And again, if you have observed the digital clinics in our community clubs, you will notice that that is almost 101, the first lesson which is provided.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But many in this minority are the elderly, the less educated and the disabled.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, although they are a minority, they must not find themselves excluded because of the phasing out of this OneKey token.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: For example, face verification can be done only if the user is physically present at these counters that the Minister has explained.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, residents who are physically disabled will find themselves having difficulty visiting the counters.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And, lastly, will residents without a recent photo on record at ICA be able to be matched by the face verification algorithm?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, in fact, that is precisely the point.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have gone to great lengths to explain how the system will work, even without access to a smart phone, without access to a mobile phone and how you can either have someone else whom you rely on as a trusted party to be the mediator of the second factor authentication as well as a new method which we call facial recognition.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My point is that we totally agree with you that we must make sure no one is excluded, that no one is worse off in the face of the inevitable progress of digital technology.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I also want to reiterate the point that I made earlier that the key thing actually is not hardware or devices, it is really trust, confidence, digital literacy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And for this, I think I will also say – and I think from all Members' experience – hand-holding is necessary.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And that is why the SG Digital Office and the more we can roll that out on the ground, accessible, so that someone is there to hold your hand and explain and teach the person, the better.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, you have my assurance that we will continue to roll this out.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And the Member's suggestion on Social Service Offices, I think we will look at it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is part of the delivery of Government services at the retail level.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Sorry, I want to make sure I answer him accurately.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I was asking for residents without a recent photo on record, how will the Government be able to match by the recognition algorithm.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think Members will also now realise why ICA has been fastidiously reminding people at a certain age to update photos so that the photo on record is a recent one.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I would also add, because Singaporeans are quite well travelled at least until 2020 came along, if all of you were to log on to your Singpass Mobile now and look at your National Digital ID, you will realise that that photograph has been updated to your latest passport photograph.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, nevertheless, your point is valid, we need to make sure we have got updated photos.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That the digital systems actually are fairly robust and are able to identify, even if we have got more eye bags, wrinkles and grey hair on our visages.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am glad to hear Minister say that physical counters will still be around to help those who really do not have the skill sets to do it, and also to minimise the risk.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They want to do it themselves rather than relying on someone to key in the Singpass password for them.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, my first supplementary question is, is there a timeline where physical counters would be phased out?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second question is, how would the Government ensure that the private sector also maintains access to services which do not require Singpass, especially for the senior citizens.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Because I get feedback from citizens, senior citizens that to open a bank account now, going to the counter with an identity card is not good enough.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They still need to go through the Singpass route.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Is there a timeline to phase out physical counters?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Now, how and where the physical counters are expressed on the ground, will vary with time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Today, the common ones we are all used to is community clubs, libraries and other suggestions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think that list would evolve but I do not see the time when we will eliminate all physical counters and human-to-human interactions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Your next point was on the private sector.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And here, this is another important question because the example that you cited – opening a bank account, it used to be that you showed up at the bank with your IC or your passport and maybe if you had, for those of us old enough to have a POSB account with stamps and all that, there was a track record, and it seemed quite seamless to open a bank account.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Actually, that same capability is available today but banks have also had to keep up with the times, both in terms of the digital possibilities which have opened up as well as the dangers of fraud and impersonation in the new world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why you will find that today, most banks, in fact all our local banks, when you actually are opening a new account, will try their best to get you to also use Singpass.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The reason why they want to use Singpass is because of this other module which we call "MyInfo".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Which means the Government as the ultimate custodian or a source of truth of trusted data that "I am who I am; I exist; my details, address and so on and so forth".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the point I am trying to make is that these are possibilities which emerge because we are a Smart Nation, because we use the digital tools available.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But even as we do this, we must make sure nobody gets left behind.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And that is why the focus on training, on hand-holding, on physical counters to get people past this hurdle.
